import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierce%E2%80%93Birkhoff_conjecture)

The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture asserts that any piecewise-polynomial function can be expressed
as a maximum of finite minima of finite collections of polynomials. It was first stated in 1956
by Garrett Birkhoff and Richard S. Pierce, though the modern rigorous formulation is due to
Melvin Henriksen and John R. Isbell.

The conjecture has been proved for `n = 1` and `n = 2` by Louis Mahé.
-/

namespace PierceBirkhoff

/--
A set is semi-algebraic in `ℝⁿ` if it can be described by a finite union of sets, each defined by
finitely many simultaneous multivariate polynomial equations and strict inequalities.
-/
def IsSemiAlgebraic {n : ℕ} (S : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (p₀ p₁ : ι → Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ)), Finite ι ∧
    S = ⋃ i, {x | (∀ p ∈ p₀ i, MvPolynomial.eval x p = 0) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ p₁ i, MvPolynomial.eval x p > 0}

/--
A set is semi-algebraic in `ℝ` if it can be described by a finite boolean combination
of polynomial equations and inequalities.
-/
def IsSemiAlgebraic₁ (S : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι₀ ι₁ : Type) (p₀ : ι₀ → Polynomial ℝ) (p₁ : ι₁ → Polynomial ℝ), Finite ι₀ ∧ Finite ι₁ ∧
    S = (⋃ i, {x | Polynomial.eval x (p₀ i) = 0}) ∪ ⋃ i, {x | Polynomial.eval x (p₁ i) > 0}

open scoped Polynomial

/--
A function `f : ℝⁿ → ℝ` is piecewise polynomial if there exists a finite covering of `ℝⁿ` by
closed semi-algebraic sets such that the restriction of `f` to each set in the covering is
polynomial.
-/
def IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (P : ι → Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (g : ι → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ),
    Finite ι ∧
    (∀ i, IsClosed (P i)) ∧
    (∀ i, IsSemiAlgebraic (P i)) ∧
    (⋃ i, P i) = Set.univ ∧
    ∀ᵉ (i : ι) (x ∈ P i), f x = MvPolynomial.eval x (g i)

/--
A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is piecewise polynomial if there exists a finite covering of `ℝ` by
closed semi-algebraic sets such that the restriction of `f` to each set in the covering is
polynomial.
-/
def IsPiecewisePolynomial (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (P : ι → Set ℝ)
    (g : ι → Polynomial ℝ),
    Finite ι ∧
    (∀ (i : ι), IsClosed (P i)) ∧
    (∀ (i : ι), IsSemiAlgebraic₁ (P i)) ∧
    (⋃ (i : ι), P i) = Set.univ ∧
    ∀ᵉ (i : ι) (x ∈ P i), f x = Polynomial.eval x (g i)

/--
The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture states that for every real piecewise-polynomial function
`f : ℝⁿ → ℝ`, there exists a finite set of polynomials `gᵢⱼ ∈ ℝ[x₁, ..., xₙ]` such that
`f = supᵢ infⱼ(gᵢⱼ)`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13]
theorem pierce_birkhoff_conjecture {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ)
    (hf : IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial f) :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type) (g : ι → κ → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ), Finite ι ∧ Finite κ ∧
      ∀ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨅ j, MvPolynomial.eval x (g i j) := by
  sorry

/--
The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture holds for `n = 1`.
This was proved by Louis Mahé.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem pierce_birkhoff_conjecture_dim_one (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : IsPiecewisePolynomial f) :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type) (g : ι → κ → Polynomial ℝ), Finite ι ∧ Finite κ ∧
      ∀ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨅ j, Polynomial.eval x (g i j) := by
  sorry

/--
The Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture holds for `n = 2`.
This was proved by Louis Mahé.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13]
theorem pierce_birkhoff_conjecture_dim_two
    (f : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf : IsPiecewiseMvPolynomial f) :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type) (g : ι → κ → MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℝ), Finite ι ∧ Finite κ ∧
      ∀ x, f x = ⨆ i, ⨅ j, MvPolynomial.eval x (g i j) := by
  sorry

end PierceBirkhoff

reformulations.difference: Uses finite unions of individual polynomial zero loci and strict-positivity loci, without explicit intersections or complements.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This characterizes all real-coefficient semialgebraic subsets of ℝ. Given a finite Boolean description, the roots of its nonzero polynomials form a finite set. Each polynomial has constant sign on every complementary interval, so the described set is a finite union of open intervals, rays, and individual points. An interval (a,b) is defined by (x-a)(b-x)>0; rays use linear strict inequalities; {a} is defined by x-a=0. Empty index types represent ∅, and the constant polynomial 1 represents ℝ by positivity. Conversely, every union allowed by the Lean definition is semialgebraic. The full equivalence was checked mathematically; Lean checks verify points, intervals, rays, and unions.

reformulations.difference: The maximum-of-minima representation uses potentially empty finite index types and one common inner index type κ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Nonempty finite real families have genuine attained maxima and minima. If either index type is empty, the Lean expression is identically zero, which also has a nonempty singleton representation using the zero polynomial. A finite family with different nonempty inner index types can be made rectangular by taking their finite product: each coordinate projection is surjective, so replacing each row by its pullback preserves its minimum. The converse uses constant inner index types. These representation equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/checks.lean as nonempty_rep_iff, rectangular_iff, and source_rep_iff.

reformulations.difference: Uses potentially empty, rectangular finite index families for its supremum-of-infima conclusion.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same representation equivalence applies to Polynomial ℝ: empty families only add a representation of zero, already represented by a singleton zero polynomial; row-dependent nonempty finite families can be replaced by their finite product without changing any minimum. The generic equivalence was proved in Lean, and the nonemptiness equivalence was explicitly specialized to univariate polynomials.

reformulations.difference: Uses potentially empty, rectangular finite index families for its supremum-of-infima conclusion.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The generic representation equivalence applies to MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℝ. Empty families only represent zero and can be replaced by singleton zero-polynomial families. Nonempty row-dependent finite families can be rectangularized using their finite product and surjective coordinate projections. Finite nonempty real extrema are the ordinary maxima and minima.

review.notes: Checked all four definitions and all three theorems. The closed-cover definitions match the primary paper exactly; Lean proofs confirm that continuity follows, so no continuity hypothesis is missing. Boundary checks cover empty semialgebraic families, singleton polynomial covers, intervals and rays, absolute value as a genuinely piecewise example, and n = 0, where every function has a constant-polynomial representation. The scratch file /workspace/review/checks.lean compiles successfully, and its key proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Wikipedia records the general problem as open and dimensions one and two as solved, matching the file. Direct access to Mahé’s publisher page and archived conference abstract was unavailable; the cited Wikipedia article and the accessible primary paper independently suffice to verify the statements and recorded statuses.
